exercises.title: Focus Block Roll-up
exercises.prompt: A study timer records consecutive focus blocks as objects with a label and a positive number of minutes. Adjacent blocks with the same label belong to one uninterrupted activity. Return a new list in which adjacent blocks with equal labels are combined by adding their minutes. Blocks with the same label that are separated by another label must remain separate, and the input must not be modified.
constraints: 0 <= blocks.length <= 10000
Each block has a non-empty string label and an integer minutes value from 1 to 1440
Labels are case-sensitive

examples.explanation: Only the first two code blocks are adjacent, so the last code block starts a new group.
An empty timeline has no groups.

exercises.title: Steady Sensor Windows
exercises.prompt: A lab sensor emits an integer reading every minute. A window is steady when the difference between its largest and smallest reading is no greater than maxSpread. Return the zero-based starting index of every steady window containing exactly width readings, in ascending order. Windows may overlap.
constraints: 1 <= readings.length <= 20000
1 <= width <= readings.length
0 <= maxSpread <= 1000000
Each reading is an integer between -1000000 and 1000000

examples.explanation: Readings [4,5,4] and [9,8,9] each have a spread of one.
Every one-reading window has a spread of zero.

exercises.title: Review Wave Planner
exercises.prompt: A release has named review tasks and dependency pairs. Each pair [before, after] means before must finish before after can start. Plan the work as simultaneous waves: every unfinished task whose dependencies are complete belongs to the next wave. Sort task names within each wave. Return all waves, or return an empty list when the dependencies contain a cycle. Tasks without dependencies still belong to the plan.
constraints: 0 <= tasks.length <= 5000
Task names are distinct non-empty strings
Every dependency names two tasks from tasks
A dependency pair contains two different task names

examples.explanation: API and docs can start together; release waits for both its direct and indirect prerequisites.
The two tasks depend on each other, so no valid wave exists.

exercises.title: Workshop Seat Allocation
exercises.prompt: Process workshop seat requests in order. Each request has a team name and a positive seat count. Accept a team's first request only when all requested seats remain, then subtract those seats. Reject every later request from a team that has already appeared, even if its first request was rejected. Other requests that do not fit are rejected for insufficient seats. Return accepted team names, rejected entries with their reason, and the seats remaining.
constraints: 0 <= capacity <= 1000000
0 <= requests.length <= 10000
Each team is a non-empty case-sensitive string
Each seats value is an integer from 1 to 1000000
Rejection reasons must be duplicate-team or insufficient-seats

examples.explanation: Lin's first request is remembered even though it could not be filled; Jo can use the two remaining seats.

exercises.title: Coverage Gap Finder
exercises.prompt: A support day covers the half-open interval [dayStart, dayEnd). Each staffed shift is another half-open interval [start, end). Clip shifts to the support day, combine overlapping or touching coverage, and return every uncovered half-open interval in chronological order. Ignore shifts that do not overlap the support day. Do not modify the shifts input.
constraints: dayStart and dayEnd are integers with dayStart < dayEnd
0 <= shifts.length <= 10000
Every shift contains integer start and end values with start < end
Input shifts may be unsorted and may extend beyond the support day

examples.explanation: The first two shifts overlap and form one coverage interval from 3 to 10.
Neither shift overlaps the half-open support day.

template is a string

capacities is sorted in nondecreasing order
Each capacity and required are integers from -1000000 to 1000000

exercises.title: Shortest Handoff Path
exercises.prompt: Services are numbered from 0 through serviceCount - 1. Each link [a, b] permits a handoff in both directions between two different services. Return the minimum number of links needed to travel from start to target, or -1 when target is unreachable. A service can appear in multiple links and the links may be given in any order.

0 <= links.length <= 10000
Every link contains two distinct service numbers in the valid range
start and target are valid service numbers

examples.explanation: The route 0 to 1 to 2 uses two links, which is shorter than going through 3 and 4.

exercises.title: Message Frequency Leaders
exercises.prompt: A message stream is represented by a list of case-sensitive labels. Count every label and return one object for each label whose count is at least threshold. Each object must contain label and count. Sort the result by count from largest to smallest, then by label in ascending ASCII order for equal counts. Return an empty list when nothing qualifies.

Each label is a non-empty string of at most 40 lowercase ASCII letters, digits, or hyphens
1 <= threshold <= 20000
Labels are compared case-sensitively

examples.explanation: Deploy has the largest count; alert is below the threshold.
Equal counts are ordered by label in ascending alphabetical order.

Bundle durations are distinct integers from 1 to 10000
Each bundle duration may be reused without limit

exercises.prompt: A mentoring map is stored as a parent array. Node 0 is the lead mentor and has parent -1; every later node names an earlier node as its direct mentor. For every node i greater than 0, 0 <= parents[i] < i

exercises.title: Threshold Pair Count
exercises.prompt: A sorted list records the signed load change from each available workshop station. Count index pairs [i, j], with i smaller than j, whose combined load is no greater than ceiling. Every value and ceiling is an integer from -1000000 to 1000000

exercises.prompt: Several services publish release events as separate sorted feeds. Each event is [time, id], every id is globally unique, and each feed is sorted by time then id. Merge all feeds and return only the ids in global order: lower time first, then ascending ASCII id when times tie. Empty feeds may appear and the input feeds must not be modified.

Each time is an integer from -1000000 to 1000000
Every id is a globally unique string of 1 to 40 ASCII letters, digits, or hyphens
Each feed is already sorted by time, then by ascending ASCII id

examples.explanation: At the shared time, ASCII orders the digit before uppercase Z and lowercase a; later events follow by time.

Reviewer names are distinct non-empty strings
Each blocked pair names two different reviewers and no unordered pair is repeated

exercises.title: Coaching Route Sums
exercises.prompt: A coaching organisation is a rooted tree stored as a parent array, with node 0 at the root and every later node attached to an earlier node. Each node has a signed score. For every query [a, b], return the sum of scores on the unique route from a to b, including both endpoints and their lowest common ancestor. Preserve query order.

parents[0] is -1; for every i greater than 0, 0 <= parents[i] < i
Each score is an integer from -1000 to 1000
0 <= queries.length <= 5000 and every queried node index is valid

examples.explanation: The first route scores 5+1+3+2; the second scores 5+1-4.
A root-to-leaf route includes every node, while a same-node route includes one score.

exercises.title: Command Message Segmentation
exercises.prompt: A compact message was formed by joining registered command tokens without separators. Recover a token sequence that reproduces the whole message using the fewest tokens. If several minimum-length sequences exist, return the lexicographically smallest token list when compared from left to right. Return an empty list for an empty message and null when no complete segmentation exists.
constraints: 0 <= tokens.length <= 1020 and 0 <= message.length <= 2000
Tokens are distinct strings of 1 to 20 lowercase ASCII letters or digits
The message contains only lowercase ASCII letters or digits
Tokens may be reused any number of times

examples.explanation: Both a+bc and ab+c use two tokens, and [a,bc] is lexicographically smaller.
The single-token reconstruction is preferred over re+view.

exercises.title: Resilient Network Budget
exercises.prompt: A practice network has numbered nodes, some free existing links, and priced repair proposals [left, right, cost]. Build a deterministic minimum-cost plan that connects every node: process proposals by ascending cost, breaking equal-cost ties by their original zero-based position, and accept a proposal only when it joins two currently separate groups. Return cost and proposalIndices in acceptance order. If full connection is impossible, return cost -1 with an empty index list.
constraints: 1 <= nodeCount <= 10000
0 <= existingLinks.length <= 10000 and 0 <= proposals.length <= 10000
Every link names two different valid node indices; duplicate endpoint pairs are allowed
Every proposal cost is an integer from 1 to 1000000

examples.explanation: The two cost-one links and proposal 4 connect all four nodes for total cost four.
Node 3 has no possible link, so no complete plan exists.

exercises.title: Delivery Receipt Ledger
exercises.prompt: A parcel rehearsal service receives receipts in arrival order. Each receipt has id, destination and units. Only the first receipt with a given id counts, even if later receipts with that id name a different destination or number of units. Total the counted units for each destination. Return objects {destination, units} sorted by destination in ascending ASCII order. Include destinations whose counted total is zero; return an empty list when there are no receipts.
constraints: 0 <= receipts.length <= 2000
id and destination are non-empty strings of at most 20 lowercase ASCII letters or digits
units is an integer from 0 to 1000; ids may repeat and destinations are case-sensitive

examples.explanation: The second r1 receipt is ignored before grouping by destination.
A counted zero-unit receipt still creates a destination in the ledger.

exercises.title: Shard Window Audit
exercises.prompt: A rehearsal ingestion service records adjustments [shard, time, delta] in no particular order. An audit query [shard, start, end] asks for the sum of deltas on that shard with start <= time < end. Return one integer per query in the original query order. Every event counts, including duplicate rows and rows at the same time. An unknown shard or an empty time window has sum zero. Negative deltas undo units and must not be discarded.
constraints: 0 <= events.length <= 2000 and 0 <= queries.length <= 2000
Shard names use 1 to 20 lowercase ASCII letters or digits
Times, start and end are integers from -10000 to 10000 with start <= end
delta is an integer from -1000 to 1000

examples.explanation: The first window includes both time-four adjustments but excludes time eight; the second window is empty.
Unsorted negative times and negative totals are valid.

exercises.title: Retry Credit Rounds
exercises.prompt: A retry rehearsal has lanes {id, refill, cap, charges}, supplied in arbitrary order. Each lane's charges list is a FIFO queue of job costs, all available from the start. Credits begin at zero. In round one and each later round, first add refill credits to every lane, capped at cap, even if that lane cannot dispatch. Then visit the lanes in ascending ASCII id order, rotated left by (round-1) modulo the number of lanes. Dispatch at most slots jobs across the entire round, and at most one job per lane. A lane can dispatch only its front job, only if it has enough credits, and only if it did not dispatch in the immediately previous round. Debit the job's charge when dispatched. A blocked lane does not consume a slot. Discard unused slots and advance the round; keep credits between rounds. Continue until every queue is empty. Return {round, lane, job} for each dispatch in emission order, where job is the original zero-based position in that lane's queue. An empty rehearsal returns an empty list. There are no arrival times or job durations to optimise.
constraints: 0 <= lanes.length <= 16 and the total number of queued jobs is at most 200
Lane ids are unique strings of 1 to 20 lowercase ASCII letters or digits
1 <= refill <= cap <= 100; charges are integers from 1 to that lane's cap
1 <= slots <= 16; round numbering starts at one and queues are never reordered

examples.explanation: Each round has one global slot. The rotated lane order and one-round cooldown alternate dispatches; the supplied order is irrelevant.
The first charge waits for credits. Rounds four and six refill credits but cooldown forbids dispatch.

exercises.title: Shard Fence Planner
exercises.prompt: An ingestion rehearsal must checkpoint an ordered sequence of events [shard, weight]. Divide the sequence into exactly batches non-empty contiguous batches, preserving event order and using every event once. The cost of a batch is its largest weight plus shardFee for each distinct shard in that batch. Return the minimum total cost. A shard appearing in several batches is charged separately in each. Return -1 if the required number of batches is impossible. An empty sequence with zero batches costs zero. Only the cost is returned, so equally good partitions need no tie-break.
constraints: 0 <= events.length <= 180 and 0 <= batches <= 20
Shard names use 1 to 20 lowercase ASCII letters or digits
weight is an integer from 1 to 1000 and shardFee is an integer from 0 to 1000

examples.explanation: The two a events cost 8+3 and the two b events cost 3+3. Other split points cost twenty.
One event cannot form two non-empty batches.

exercises.title: Panel Notice Counters
exercises.prompt: A practice dashboard receives events [panel, action] in order. All panels begin with zero unread notices. A notify event increments that panel's count by one. A read event clears that panel's count to zero, even if it has not appeared before. After all events, return objects {panel, unread} for panels with a positive count, sorted by panel in ascending ASCII order. Reading one panel must not clear any other panel, and future notices after a read start counting again.
constraints: 0 <= events.length <= 2000
Panel names use 1 to 20 lowercase ASCII letters or digits
Every action is exactly notify or read

examples.explanation: The earlier z notice was read, but the later z notice is unread. Neither read affects a.
The final read clears the only notice; zero-count panels are omitted.

exercises.title: Draft Revision Fold
exercises.prompt: A rehearsal editor receives full draft updates {id, revision, text} in delivery order, not revision order. For each id, accept its first update and then only updates with a strictly larger revision. Equal revisions keep the first accepted text. A null text is a deletion marker: retain its revision when rejecting stale updates, but omit that draft from the final output. A later larger revision with non-null text restores the draft. Return the accepted non-deleted drafts as {id, revision, text} sorted by id in ascending ASCII order. Empty text is a live draft, not a deletion.
constraints: 0 <= updates.length <= 2000
ids use 1 to 20 lowercase ASCII letters or digits; revision is an integer from 0 to 10000
text is null or an ASCII string of at most 80 characters

examples.explanation: The stale update cannot resurrect a, and b keeps the first text at revision one.
An empty string remains live and b is restored by a larger revision.

exercises.title: Viewport Anchor Walk
exercises.prompt: A rehearsal reading view stacks panels with positive integer pixel heights in fixed order. Its anchor starts at panel zero, inset zero. Process commands in order. A jump command ["jump", offset] moves to an absolute zero-based pixel offset in the current stack, clamped to the first or last pixel if outside it. A resize command ["resize", panelIndex, height] changes one height while keeping the anchor's panel and inset; if the anchor's panel shrinks below its inset, clamp the inset to its last pixel. Resizing an earlier panel does not change which pixel within the anchored panel is followed. Return [panelIndex, inset] after every command. At an exact boundary a jump lands on the next panel at inset zero.
constraints: 1 <= heights.length <= 400 and 0 <= commands.length <= 400
All initial and resized heights are integers from 1 to 1000; resize indices are valid
Jump offsets are integers from -1000000 to 1000000

examples.explanation: The jump anchors six pixels into panel one. Shrinking it clamps to one; resizing panel zero keeps that anchor.
The boundary belongs to panel one. Out-of-range jumps clamp against the resized stack.

exercises.title: Focus Shortcut Tour
exercises.prompt: A keyboard-navigation rehearsal numbers its panels from zero to panelCount-1. Each directed shortcut [from, to, effort] moves focus with the given effort; it does not imply a reverse shortcut. Starting at panel zero, find the least total effort of a walk that visits every panel in required at least once and ends at panelCount-1. Required panels may be visited in any order. A walk may revisit panels or pass through the final panel before finishing there. Merely passing through a required panel counts as a visit. Choose the cheaper shortcut when several join the same ordered pair. Return -1 when no such walk exists, otherwise return its cost only. Visiting the starting panel needs no move.
constraints: 1 <= panelCount <= 40 and 0 <= shortcuts.length <= 1600
0 <= required.length <= 10; required contains distinct valid panel indices
Shortcuts have valid distinct endpoints and integer effort from 0 to 1000; duplicate directed pairs are allowed

examples.explanation: Focus moves 0 to 2 to 1 to 3 for effort four; required order does not prescribe visit order.
The finish is reachable but required panel one is not.
